briefing:
EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
The Middle East situation remains volatile, marked by a declared de-escalation between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon, which was immediately followed by renewed hostilities and conflicting statements from leadership. This period saw exceptionally harsh exchanges between US President Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, while Iran escalated its rhetoric, linking the Lebanese front to its own ceasefire with the US and threatening key shipping lanes.

IRAN
Iran's internal political situation saw discussions around the final text of a draft Iranian proposal, which remains under review in Tehran due to "history of US commitment violations and suspicion." The internet in Iran reportedly experienced a "partial reopening" but remains unstable, with users experiencing widespread mobile and internet outages in southern provinces. Economically, a currency exchange company in Isfahan was dissolved for economic disruption. The IRGC announced that two of its members, Hussein Ramazanian Fardoui and Mohammad Oveysi, were killed in Qom by "unexploded ordnance from the war with Israel and the US," a claim of internal casualties from unspecified past conflict. Militarily, the IRGC Navy claimed to have struck the US-Israeli linked vessel "MSC Sariska" with a cruise missile in a retaliatory operation after an alleged US attack on the Iranian commercial vessel "Lian Star" in the Sea of Oman. This claim lacks independent verification. Iran's Quds Force Commander Brigadier General Esmail Qa'ani warned that continued Israeli aggression in Lebanon and Gaza, supported by the US, would "activate other fronts" and make the Bab al-Mandab Strait mirror traffic restrictions in the Strait of Hormuz. Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf stated that if Israeli crimes continue in Lebanon, Iran will not only halt dialogue with the US but also "stand firmly against them." Iran's Foreign Ministry announced a suspension of indirect message exchanges with the US in protest of Israeli operations in Lebanon. Press TV reported that Iranian retaliatory attacks have damaged at least 20 US military sites, according to satellite imagery analysis.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations in the Gaza Strip resulted in the killing of five terror operatives identified as Salem Qariqa (Hamas Shejaiya Battalion, explosives/sniping), Saeed Shamali (Hamas Nukhba Force team commander), Ahmad Khallas (PIJ sniper platoon commander), and two additional Hamas commanders involved in planting bombs. Jamal Abu Aoun, a Hamas platoon commander and doctor at Yafa Hospital in Deir al-Balah, was also killed. In Lebanon, Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester, 30, a medical officer with the Givati Brigade's Shaked Battalion, was killed by a Hezbollah explosive drone attack in southern Lebanon. Seven other soldiers were wounded in the same incident, including two officers and one soldier seriously. Israel conducted strikes in southern Lebanon, killing Mohammed Mousa Mteirek, a unit commander in Hezbollah's missile array, in the Nabatieh area. Israeli Air Force also killed three Hezbollah operatives north of the Litani River who were preparing to launch drones. The IDF withdrew the 146th Division from southern Lebanon after three months, with the 91st and 36th Divisions remaining. On the home front, the Home Front Command extended rocket warning times for 161 communities in Northern Israel, Haifa, Krayot, and Carmel from 60 to 90 seconds, effective 02 June 2026, 16:00 UTC. Air defense systems intercepted two rockets near Safed and one near Kiryat Shmona, and three rockets near Karmiel. A Hezbollah drone struck a military position in the Western Galilee, and another FPV drone struck Rosh Hanikra. Politically, US President Donald Trump reportedly "attacked with curses" Prime Minister Netanyahu during a phone call, expressing anger over Israel's planned escalation in Lebanon and stating, "You're fucking crazy. You'd be in prison if it weren't for me. I’m saving your ass. Everybody hates you now. Everybody hates Israel because of this." Netanyahu publicly stated that if Hezbollah does not cease attacks, Israel will strike terror targets in Beirut, while continuing operations in Southern Lebanon. The Knesset approved a bill to dissolve the 25th Knesset, moving towards early elections between 08 September and 20 October. A bill to split the Attorney General's role passed its first reading. Ultra-Orthodox protests over mandatory enlistment blocked roads, including Highway 4 and railway tracks near Gannot, and attempted to enter the home of the head of the police traffic department. One protester was seriously injured. France announced it would ban Israel from the Eurosatory defense exhibition in Paris, drawing a strong rebuke from the Israeli Ministry of Defense. The Supreme Court (Bagatz) approved the appointment of Roman Gofman as the new Mossad chief, rejecting challenges and critically assessing the Attorney General's previous stance.

GAZA & WEST BANK
In the Gaza Strip, Israeli forces killed five terror operatives from Hamas and Palestinian Islamic Jihad (PIJ) who were preparing attacks against Israeli troops. Additionally, Jamal Abu Aoun, a Hamas platoon commander operating as a doctor, was killed for advancing and planning terror attacks. Israeli forces operated in Hebron at the home of a terrorist who carried out a ramming attack. Hamas welcomed the UN blacklisting of Israel for sexual violence. Hardline Israeli Finance Minister Bezalel Smotrich called for dismantling the Palestinian Authority and seizing the entire occupied West Bank.

LEBANON
Hezbollah continued cross-border operations, claiming 41 retaliatory strikes in 24 hours and targeting six Israeli Merkava tanks. An explosive drone attack killed an IDF medical officer, Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester, and wounded seven other soldiers in southern Lebanon. Hezbollah launched rockets and drones toward Israeli communities, triggering sirens in Safed, Western Galilee, Rosh Hanikra, Metula, Kiryat Shmona, and Karmiel. Israel responded with strikes, killing Hezbollah missile commander Mohammed Mousa Mteirek in Nabatieh and three operatives north of the Litani. Israeli forces operating in southern Lebanon continue to hold the Beaufort Castle area, a key Hezbollah stronghold from which over 400 launches were conducted since the "Lion's Roar" operation. The IDF issued evacuation warnings to residents of Beirut's Dahiyeh area, threatening strikes if Hezbollah continues firing rockets at Israeli cities. US President Trump announced an agreement for Israel to halt a planned "major raid of Beirut" and for Hezbollah to cease firing at Israel; however, this was immediately followed by renewed rocket fire from Lebanon and conflicting statements. Lebanese MP Hassan Fadlallah stated that Hezbollah rejects any "unilateral" or partial ceasefire, insisting on a comprehensive halt to hostilities across all Lebanese territory, including Israeli withdrawal. The UN World Food Programme reported that approximately 1.24 million people in Lebanon (one in four) face acute food insecurity.

SYRIA & IRAQ
Russia sent aid and supplies to its Khmeimim air base on Syria's coast, the first time since the fall of the Assad regime, indicating preparations for continued control under the future government of Ahmad al-Shara. A Syrian citizen, Khaled, is on trial in Vienna, Austria, accused of being Assad's intelligence chief in Raqqa and involvement in murder and abuse. In Iraq, a commercial vessel was attacked twice near Umm Qasr in the Persian Gulf, with one incident attributed to a drone. An explosion in Baghdad's Rusafeh district was reported, with initial indications of a grenade attack on a home. An alleged hacker offered 750,000 Korek Telecom subscriber data for sale on the dark web. As'hab al-Kahf, an Iraqi militia, threatened Eilat in the occupied territories as an operational zone if Beirut's Dahiyeh is attacked. Syria reportedly earned up to $5.9 million in May from a 375% increase in air traffic over its airspace following the Iran war, charging $499 per flight.

GULF STATES
The US intercepted two ballistic missiles launched by Iran towards an American base in Kuwait. Oman is reportedly under pressure from the Trump administration to choose sides and cut diplomatic ties with Iran, with US officials viewing Oman's neutrality as hostile. Trump reportedly threatened to bomb Oman if it proceeds with charging transit fees in the Strait of Hormuz. The Strait of Hormuz remained a focal point of tension; Iran and the "Resistance Front" declared an intent to close it and activate other fronts, including Bab al-Mandab. The Persian Gulf Strait Authority, established by Iran, claimed to have processed over 300 non-Iranian vessel transit requests since early May and coordinated the passage of 15 ships (including four oil tankers) in the past 24 hours. Trump asked NATO allies for assistance in securing the Strait of Hormuz, citing their reliance on its oil. Qatar's Foreign Minister discussed regional developments and maritime security with Iran's Foreign Minister, reiterating Qatar's full support for a comprehensive agreement to end the crisis.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1. **Lebanese Ceasefire and Immediate Violations**: US President Trump announced a mutual cessation of hostilities between Israel and Hezbollah in Lebanon, with Israel agreeing not to attack Beirut and Hezbollah agreeing to stop firing at Israel. However, this was immediately followed by renewed rocket fire from Lebanon and conflicting statements from Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu, who maintained Israel would strike Beirut if attacks continue, while continuing operations in Southern Lebanon.
2. **Heated US-Israel Leadership Exchange**: US President Trump reportedly "attacked with curses" Prime Minister Netanyahu during a telephone call, accusing him of being "fucking crazy" and putting Israel at global risk due to planned escalation in Lebanon.
3. **IDF Casualty in Southern Lebanon**: Cpt. Dr. Ori Yosef Silvester, 30, an IDF medical officer, was killed in southern Lebanon by a Hezbollah explosive drone, and seven other Israeli soldiers were wounded, with two officers and one soldier sustaining serious injuries.
4. **Iranian Escalation and Threats**: Iran suspended indirect talks with the US in protest of Israeli actions in Lebanon and threatened to close the Strait of Hormuz and activate the Bab al-Mandab Strait if Israeli aggression continues. The IRGC Navy claimed to have struck the US-Israeli linked vessel "MSC Sariska" with a cruise missile in retaliation for an alleged US attack on an Iranian commercial vessel.
5. **Increased Israeli Home Front Preparedness**: Israel's Home Front Command extended rocket warning times for 161 communities in Northern Israel, Haifa, Krayot, and Carmel, from 60 to 90 seconds, effective 02 June 2026, 16:00 UTC.
6. **Ultra-Orthodox Protests in Israel**: Thousands of ultra-Orthodox individuals protested against mandatory military enlistment, blocking major roads and railway lines, leading to clashes with police and one serious injury.
7. **Russian Military Resupply to Syria**: Russia sent military aid and supplies to its Khmeimim air base in Syria, marking the first such delivery since the fall of the Assad regime, indicating a strategic posture for continued influence in the region.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
Escalation risks on the Israel-Lebanon front remain critically high despite any declared de-escalation; the immediate resumption of hostilities and conflicting statements indicate continued military engagement is likely. Hezbollah's rejection of a partial ceasefire, demanding a full Israeli withdrawal, sets a high bar for any sustainable calm. Iran's explicit threat to close the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab in response to Israeli actions in Lebanon, coupled with its claimed naval strike on a US-Israeli linked vessel, represents a significant escalation flashpoint with global economic implications. The direct, acrimonious communication between US President Trump and PM Netanyahu suggests a strain in alliance leadership that could impact coordinated responses to regional threats. Internally, ongoing ultra-Orthodox protests in Israel, fueled by the conscription issue and broader government policies, pose a flashpoint for domestic instability and societal friction.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
**United States**: President Trump publicly announced a de-escalation in Lebanon but reportedly had an extremely hostile conversation with PM Netanyahu. The US also intercepted two ballistic missiles aimed at its Kuwaiti base. Discussions are underway within the US regarding extending nuclear military deployments to other European NATO countries, specifically Poland.
**European Union**: EU ambassadors are set to discuss sanctions against Israeli ministers, including Itamar Ben Gvir, requiring a unanimous vote with uncertainty about Czech Republic's stance. France banned Israel from the Eurosatory defense exhibition, drawing strong condemnation from Israel. The UK is stockpiling multi-purpose missiles in anticipation of potential Iranian drone attacks. Germany's Chancellor Friedrich Merz plans to host European leaders and the NATO Secretary-General to formulate a joint strategy to soften relations with Trump ahead of the July NATO summit in Ankara.
**Russia**: Russia sent military supplies to its Khmeimim base in Syria, signaling continued operational presence. In Ukraine, Russia launched extensive air attacks on Kyiv and Dnipro, resulting in multiple casualties. Russia criticized the "unjustified American and Israeli aggression against Iran" as a direct cause of Lebanon's deteriorating situation during a UN Security Council meeting.
**China**: China's representative to the UN Security Council called for Israel to immediately cease military operations and respect Lebanon's sovereignty and territorial integrity.
**Canada**: Prime Minister Mark Carney announced the formation of a new federal advisory council to combat antisemitism, stating that antisemitism in Canada has reached levels unseen since WWII.
**Gulf States**: Qatar's Foreign Minister engaged in phone consultations with Iran's Foreign Minister, discussing regional developments and maritime security, and reiterated support for a comprehensive agreement to resolve the crisis. Oman faces US pressure to cut diplomatic ties with Iran, with threats of bombing if it charges Strait of Hormuz transit fees.
**Pakistan**: Pakistan's Permanent Representative to the UN condemned Israeli attacks on Lebanon as a "blatant violation of international law," holding Israel responsible for undermining peace efforts.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Significant contradictions exist regarding the announced ceasefire/de-escalation in Lebanon. President Trump's declaration of an agreement for mutual cessation of fire was immediately undermined by renewed rocket fire from Lebanon and PM Netanyahu's subsequent statement affirming Israel's right to strike Beirut if Hezbollah attacks continue. Hezbollah, through MP Hassan Fadlallah, explicitly rejected a partial ceasefire, demanding a comprehensive halt to hostilities and Israeli withdrawal.

The IRGC's claim of striking the "MSC Sariska" with a cruise missile in retaliation for an alleged US attack on the "Lian Star" lacks independent confirmation from other sources. While UKMTO reported a commercial vessel collision near Umm Qasr, Iraq, with a subsequent fire, no connection to an IRGC cruise missile attack or US aggression was made.

Reports from SharghDaily and VahidOnline on internet connectivity in Iran contradict official narratives of full restoration, noting a "partial and unstable" return, with widespread outages across several southern provinces, suggesting ongoing state control or disruption.

The reported harsh language used by President Trump toward PM Netanyahu, detailed by "two senior American officials and another source," highlights a severe diplomatic strain.

The claim of two IRGC members killed in Qom by "unexploded ordnance from the war with Israel and the US" is unusual phrasing, as Qom has not been a direct combat zone in any recent conflict involving Israel or the US, raising questions about the actual circumstances of their deaths.

The Wall Street Journal report, cited by N12, that the US threatened to bomb Oman over Strait of Hormuz fees, while attributed to "American and Arab officials," is an unverified claim of highly aggressive US intent.

There is a reporting gap on the specific details and ongoing status of diplomatic exchanges between Iran and the US, beyond Iran's stated suspension of indirect talks. The extent and nature of US and Qatari mediation efforts remain opaque.
